environment.description: Same provider binary deployed on an EC2 instance in a private subnet (no IGW route) within an AWS Organization member account. The instance role has IAMFullAccess BUT the Organization has an SCP (id: p-restrict-iam-dangerous) attached at the OU level that contains a Deny statement with Condition checking that the calling principal's ARN does NOT match the automation role pattern. Additionally, the IAM user/role executing has a permission boundary (arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:policy/TerraformProviderBoundary) that explicitly denies iam:CreateRole, iam:PutRolePolicy, iam:AttachRolePolicy, iam:DeleteRole UNLESS the resource ARN matches 'arn:aws:iam::*:role/terraform/tf-managed-readonly-*'. The permission boundary uses a StringNotLike condition on iam:PermissionsBoundary requiring any created role to also have the same boundary attached. The SCP separately denies iam:PutRolePolicy where the policy document contains '"Effect":"Allow"' combined with '"Resource":"*"' and '"Action":"*"' (using StringLike on iam:PolicyDocument). Security group on the instance only allows inbound from 127.0.0.1/32 on port 19443.

config.scp_effect: Deny on iam:PutRolePolicy when policy document matches *Effect*Allow*Resource*star*Action*star* via StringLike condition
config.permission_boundary_effect: Deny iam:CreateRole, iam:PutRolePolicy, iam:AttachRolePolicy, iam:DeleteRole UNLESS resource matches arn:aws:iam::*:role/terraform/tf-managed-readonly-* AND created role must have same boundary attached
config.network: private subnet, no IGW, no NAT for inbound
